title: LLM landscape actionable snapshots for Sales + SRE
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Objective: Produce a repeatable, easily digestible weekly snapshot of the open and commercial LLM landscape tailored to two operational audiences: Sales (deal enablement) and SRE/Platform (fallback planning and latency budgeting).

Rationale: Sales needs concise competitive signals (cost delta, model availability, contractual constraints, known quality regressions) to shape deal conversations. SRE needs concrete, engineer-friendly metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, queuing characteristics, batching compatibility, quantization readiness) and a short list of tested fallback pairs with measured impact. Current landscape reports are too long and not actionable for either audience.

Deliverables: (1) One-page Sales snapshot with 6 KPIs per vendor/model and recommended sales talking points; (2) One-page SRE snapshot with latency buckets, quant-compatibility flags, and a 3-step fallback recipe; (3) Machine-readable CSV/JSON export for ingestion into internal dashboards; (4) Short how-to playbook for on-call use during model outages.

Method: Combine telemetry (synthetic p99 latency runs across regions), contract metadata (rate limits, SLA language), model-interop tests (tokenization/parity tests, structured output compatibility), and field reports from Solutions and GTM. Automate weekly synthetic checks hitting representative request templates and collect result artifacts to S3 and the market-snapshot dashboard.

Audience & consumption: Sales gets a PDF + short Slack thread with two highlighted lines per account segment; SRE gets a dashboard tile with top-3 risky model variants and a one-click runbook that triggers canary reroute to the tested fallback variant.

Scope exclusions: No deep model quality evaluation beyond a small set of prompt families. This ticket focuses on operational signals and procurement implications, not full accuracy benchmarks or legal contract negotiation.

Success metrics: adoption by GTM reps (>= 10 reps using snapshot in first two weeks), reduced time-to-fallback during simulated outage drills (target: from 18m to <8m), and ingestion of snapshot export into the Console signals feed.

Retention of artifacts and traceability: snapshots stored in Confluence page 'Market Snapshot / Weekly' and raw CSV exports in drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1MarketSnapshots. Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/market-snapshots. PRs and test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/market-snapshot-harness/pulls
acceptance_criteria: One-page Sales PDF template produced and reviewed by two GTM reps with sign-off comment in Confluence
SRE one-pager and three validated fallback recipes executed in staging with measured p99 impact recorded
Automated weekly synthetic runner committed to the repository and scheduled in CI with sample output for at least 5 model variants
CSV/JSON export schema documented and consumed by market-snapshot dashboard with at least one visual tile showing p99 by region
Runbook and Slack escalation snippet published and linked from the Console's model health panel

risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Snapshot exposes contractual details that Legal deems sensitive. Mitigation: redact contract-specific language and represent only normalized flags (e.g., 'rate-limited-during-peaks').

Risk: Synthetic probes might not reflect real customer workloads and could generate false positives. Mitigation: include a small set of telemetry-based checks using anonymized customer latency percentiles to validate signal drift.
Risk: Team bandwidth for weekly maintenance. Mitigation: build a simple scheduler and a lightweight alert if job fails; handoff doc for on-call runbook.
Risk: Overfitting Sales messaging to current model set. Mitigation: include a one-line 'confidence' score per snapshot and an explicit refresh cadence (weekly) plus manual override.
